newsitem.title: UK: Severn Trent up on buyback news, results.
newsitem.headline: Severn Trent up on buyback news, results.

text.p: Shares in Severn Trent Plc firmed in pre-market trade on Tuesday, buoyed by the British water and sewerage company's plans to complete a share buyback announced last year, dealers said.
The shares were five pence higher at 775p by 0715 GMT.
The company announced annual pre-exceptional pre-tax profits of 391 million stg, compared with forecasts of 381 to 395 million.
"The results were pretty much in line with forecasts, maybe slightly towards the top end," said Simon Champion, analyst at Charterhouse Tilney.
"There were no surprises in there. But the profits were above some people's forecasts, and they also announced they were completing their share buyback."
Champion said utility companies were unlikely to announce any surprise moves until they found out the level of the windfall tax which the new Labour government plans to levy on them.
"The results were good although not unexpected, but the buyback news has helped the shares," a market-maker said.

The company announced last year that it would buy back up to 10 percent of its shares and bought 5.6 percent in December 1996. It said on Tuesday it would complete thebuyback if appproved by its annual meeting.
Other shares in the sector were mostly unchanged, although Yorkshire Water Plc climbed two pence to 374-1/2 and Thames Water Plc edged up 1/2p to 689. Hyder Plc slipped two pence to 822-1/2.
